A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ModalPrompt research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, allowing reliable matching across substantial rewriting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original CoIN benchmark results, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and detailed continual-learning trajectories in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, encoder studies, and Qwen-VL results in Section 4 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The frozen backbone, learned projection, and top-k prompt fusion/selection are retained. The stated prototype loss changes from duplicated text-similarity terms in v1 Eq. 12 to image-plus-text similarity in v2 Eq. 6. This is a limited objective correction; whether the implementation changed is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight CoIN datasets covering question answering, classification, and grounding. The new encoder experiment uses a subset of these datasets, while Qwen-VL introduces a different model configuration without extending data or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds L2P, Dualprompt, and CODA-Prompt to the main comparison, and LWF, EWC, and Model Tailor in Appendix C. CODA-Prompt also enters the stagewise, efficiency, and prompt-count comparisons. v1's appendix comparator named CoIN corresponds to the retained MoELoRA baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen-VL evaluation, six-dataset encoder comparisons using CLIP/L with BPE and CLIP/G for both modalities, and prompt/expert-count sweeps across methods. The original CoIN task order and metric formulas remain: Last and Avg rename ContinualT and CAA.

E4.justification: v2 adds encoder sensitivity testing and extends prompt-count analysis to MoELoRA and CODA-Prompt. Existing component ablations gain longitudinal metrics. Conversely, v1's study of selecting one, two, or three prompt sets disappears. The similarity maps, selection maps, and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. Averaging accuracy across tasks does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive baseline, encoder, and Qwen-VL results while retaining ModalPrompt's main final-task scores. Existing values also change: multi-task ScienceQA rises from 46.22 to 81.43, and appendix final VQAv2/OCRVQA entries change from 65.02/57.59 to 66.90/59.68, matching the main table. The control-score revisions lack an explanation of changed settings.

T1.justification: The visual projection's dimensional mapping is corrected from text-to-vision dimensions in v1 Eq. 4 to vision-to-text dimensions in v2 Eq. 1, alongside the prototype-loss correction. These are local mathematical corrections. The explicit O(T)/O(k) notation restates the existing complexity argument, and renamed evaluation metrics retain their formulas.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions replace the headline +20% improvement with +14.26%, reflecting the Avg comparison against CODA-Prompt. The central contribution of multimodally guided prompt fusion and selection, and the claimed 1.42-fold inference speed, remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges limited forward transfer to unseen tasks. Appendix C adds explanations for retaining CLIP/L and interprets Qwen-VL results as architectural generalizability. The explanation of interference when selecting two versus one or three prompt sets disappears with that analysis.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release; v2 states that code is available and supplies a ModalPrompt URL. Appendices B–D add instruction templates, baseline configurations such as MoELoRA's eight experts and rank 16, a LLaVA repository reference, and the GPU's 48 GB capacity. These substantially expand documented reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Related work shifts from a broad continual-learning taxonomy toward continual instruction tuning and multimodal adaptation. It adds substantial literature, including MaPLe, M2PT, conditional LoRA, and HIDE-LLaVA, while removing several generic replay references. Appendix C additionally positions the method against Model Tailor and regularization approaches.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method, and results undergo extensive rewriting. The method is reorganized into guidance features, training-time fusion, and inference-time selection. Metric definitions move to Appendix A, appendices are reorganized by function, and limitations, ethical impact, and acknowledgments sections are added.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, replaces the introductory radar chart with a conceptual diagram, and redraws the method figure. It merges and relabels the heatmaps, restructures benchmark and ablation tables, and adds notation, instruction, comparison, and trajectory tables plus a Qwen-VL radar chart.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important validation gap: v1's prompt-based method was compared primarily with Finetune and MoELoRA. Relevant prompt baselines, broader controls, encoder/backbone checks, and expanded technical disclosure substantially strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. These gains outweigh the removed selection-count analysis and remaining reporting problems, including Finetune B8 being 31.16 in Table 4 versus approximately 35.61 calculated from Table 10.
